pharm: Diphenylmethylpiperazine calcium-entry blocker with antihistamine (H1) activity
quick: 10 mg once daily at night (5 mg if elderly/over 65)
Take in the evening; food not essential
No specific adjustment; use with caution
summary: Flunarizine is a selective calcium-entry blocker with additional antihistaminic properties used principally for migraine prophylaxis and for symptomatic treatment of vestibular vertigo. Treatment is typically given once daily at night and reassessed regularly because of cumulative risks of sedation, weight gain, depression, and extrapyramidal effects. Continuous use is generally limited to around six months.
indications: Prophylaxis of migraine (when other treatments are unsuitable or ineffective)
Symptomatic treatment of vestibular vertigo (peripheral and central)

dosage.d: 10 mg once daily in the evening
dosage.n: Reassess after about 2 months; max continuous use ~6 months then review

dosage.d: 5 mg once daily in the evening
dosage.n: Lower dose due to higher risk of extrapyramidal effects and sedation

dosage.d: 10 mg once daily (5 mg in elderly); continue until symptoms controlled, then stop
dosage.n: Discontinue once symptoms resolve; review need regularly

admin: Take once daily, preferably in the evening, to limit daytime drowsiness
Swallow with water; food not required
Do not exceed recommended treatment duration without review (typically max ~6 months continuous)
Reassess efficacy after about 2 months in migraine prophylaxis
Discontinue if depression, parkinsonism, or excessive weight gain develop
moa: Selectively blocks calcium entry through cellular calcium channels, preventing pathological cellular calcium overload, with additional antagonism at histamine H1 receptors. These actions are thought to stabilise vascular and vestibular neuronal function, reducing migraine frequency and vertigo. The antidopaminergic component contributes to its extrapyramidal side-effect profile.

absolute: Parkinson's disease or other extrapyramidal disorders
Pre-existing symptoms of depression or extrapyramidal disorder
relative: Elderly patients (increased risk of sedation and parkinsonism)

preg: Adequate human data are lacking; avoid during pregnancy unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk and only under specialist advice.
lact: Flunarizine is expected to be excreted in breast milk; breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is established; use with general caution.
hepatic: Flunarizine is extensively metabolised by the liver; use with caution in hepatic impairment and consider lower doses.

major: CNS depressants and sedatives - additive sedation
moderate: Antipsychotics / dopamine antagonists - additive extrapyramidal effects
Hypnotics, anxiolytics, tricyclic antidepressants - enhanced sedation
CYP enzyme inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, phenytoin) - may reduce flunarizine levels
minor: No other clinically significant interactions established
interactions.food: No clinically important food interaction; may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol due to enhanced sedation and drowsiness
interactions.diagnostics: No significant laboratory test interference reported

monitoring: Treatment duration and need to continue
counsel: Take once daily in the evening as it can cause drowsiness
Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you
Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine
Tell your doctor about any low mood, depression, tremor, or stiffness
Weight gain is common; monitor diet and activity
Do not stop abruptly without advice; treatment is usually time-limited and reviewed
pk: Long; approximately 18-19 days at steady state
Store below 25-30°C, protect from light and moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; record based on EMA/SmPC/BNF sources; pending clinical review.
Long elimination half-life means steady state and side effects accumulate over weeks; effects may persist after stopping
Continuous use is generally limited to about 6 months with periodic review to limit extrapyramidal risk
Contraindicated in patients with a history of depression or Parkinson's disease
Elderly patients are particularly susceptible to sedation, depression, and parkinsonism - use the 5 mg dose
Discontinue if depression, parkinsonism, or significant weight gain develops
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered the same evening; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual once-daily schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Reported features of overdose include sedation, agitation, and tachycardia. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive and symptomatic with monitoring. Activated charcoal may be considered if presentation is early. Because of the long half-life, observe for prolonged or delayed effects.
